title: Application of Mediation Mixture Modeling and Machine Learning to Understand Heterogeneity of Risk Pathways on Youth's Onset of Substance Use
text:
This study will use newly developed methodological approaches to understand the heterogeneity of key
mediation pathways from parent mental health to early initiation of substance use among youth via their
externalizing and internalizing spectrums. The study also investigates the distinctive links among genetic,
family and environmental contextual factors and the enumerated heterogeneous mediation pathways.
Elucidating the heterogeneity of these mediation pathways will identify specific risk mechanisms to increase
the accuracy of identifying at-risk groups for substance use to inform preventive personalized intervention.

title: REGULATION OF ATROPHY-INDUCED PROGENITOR CELLS IN THE GASTRIC CORPUS
text:
The process by which stem cells differentiate into parietal cells in the stomach lining is poorly understood, yet it
underlies a variety of human health conditions, including Helicobacter pylori infection, peptic ulcers,
gastroesophageal reflux disease, autoimmune gastritis, chronic atrophic gastritis, pyloric metaplasia, and
gastric cancers. We aim to characterize the molecular and cellular steps involved in this differentiation process,
define how ERRγ and other factors are critical for healthy parietal cell function, and establish utility for those
factors in therapeutic approaches that could be developed for the treatment of conditions related to abnormal
parietal cell abundance and activity.

title: Identifying differences in dynamics and residual structure of intrinsically disordered domains between monomer and fibers: using alpha-synuclein as a model
text:
Synucleinopathies, including Parkinson's disease, are progressive neurodegenerative diseases that affect
thousands of people each year. It is imperative to study the flexible regions of α-synuclein, the misfolded protein
associated with these diseases, as research has demonstrated that they influence disease severity. My findings
will provide insight on the molecular features that will help us understand harmful cellular interactions and
toxicity in misfolded α-synuclein.

title: AI-Enabled ComPLETE Model for Better Prediction of CLTIRevascularization Outcomes
text:
Patients with chronic limb threatening ischemia (CLTI) – a severe vascular condition that tends to impact older
adults with multiple comorbidities – must undergo revascularization surgery to manage this condition and
typically face a difficult recovery after hospital discharge with a high likelihood of experiencing complications and
hospital readmission. We seek to better understand the factors that contribute to these high rates of poor
outcomes by collecting and combining several data sources, including surveys, Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based
mobile health data, and electronic health record data. We will subsequently use AI-based machine learning
models to determine the most significant predictive factors of poor CLTI revascularization outcomes, with a focus
on those that are amenable to intervention.

title: Michigan Center on the Demography of Aging
text: MiCDA promotes research on the demography of aging, focusing on issues related to the changing demography of late-life disability, dementia and family caregiving; the social, environmental and biological underpinnings over the life course that shape later-life health and wellbeing; and related advances in data infrastructure and methods. Findings contribute to the understanding of the health and wellbeing of older adults in the context of an aging US population.

title: Toward a Curative Treatment for HBV with cccDNA-Targeting Peptide Nucleic Acids
text:
Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is an incurable viral infection of the liver that causes hepatocarcinoma
and cirrhosis. Even when treated with the best available drugs, HBV causes other long-term health
problems for patients because of a persistent viral genome known as covalently closed circular DNA, or
cccDNA. To eliminate cccDNA and cure HBV, this proposal creates a group of compounds known as
peptide nucleic acids and tests their ability to target and degrade cccDNA in animal models of HBV.

title: Mouse Genetics
text: The primary role of Mouse Genetics Core Facility (MGCF) is to facilitate the use of mouse molecular genetics at MSK for in vivo studies of gene functions germane to cancer. Relevant fields in which MSK investigators develop and apply mouse models include: cell growth and behavior, stem cell biology, embryonic development, immunobiology, genome integrity, cancer biology, and experimental therapeutics. The expertise of MGCF covers three broad areas pertaining to the generation and effective use of genetically engineered mouse (GEM) models—namely, molecular and cell biology, embryo micromanipulation, and reproductive biology. The molecular and cellular biology services cover design and assembly of genome engineering reagents, such as donor transgenes and CRISPR/Cas9; performing all aspects of gene targeting in mouse embryonic stem (ES) cells; identification and verification of alleles carried by a generated GEM model; and establishment of new ES cells from a variety of GEM lines. Reagents and materials generated in the molecular and cellular biology arm of services are brought to the embryology platform for introduction of transgene or genome editing reagents into zygotes and microinjection of ES cells into host embryos. Services in the reproductive biology arm complement the efficient use of GEM resources, including cryopreservation and long-term storage of GEM lines, strain recovery and propagation through IVF and embryo transfer, furnishing special embryological and surgical procedures, and provision of special GEM lines such as drug resistance gene and fluorescent reporter expressing strains. The Core also has an integral role in collaboratively providing consultation and training for the design and production of GEM models, ES cell culture and manipulation, and mouse reproduction and genetic crosses. Rapid advances in genome editing and sequencing technologies, in combination with the steady increase in translational research at MSK, have resulted in an increasing demand for GEM models supported by the MGCF services. In addition, MGCF continues to pursue and implement new technical developments that will expedite transgenesis and genome editing in mice. Ongoing efforts are centered on combining various new genome editing tools and methodologies to efficiently engineer large and complex genetic alleles in vivo. Integrating such advances into the Core’s services will lead to increased productivity and aid in efficient creation of innovative GEM models for MSK investigators. The MGCF has supported at least 600 publications in the reporting period of 2018-2024, including 266 considered high-impact.

title: Mapping the origin of HER2 plasticity in breast cancer
text:
Some breast cancers across molecular subtypes harbor low levels of HER2 expression, and recent clinical studies
show that in some cases, these tumors are responsive to HER2-targeted antibody drug conjugates. Patient HER+
and HER2- circulating tumor cells can rapidly interconvert in the absence of genomic alterations, suggesting an
epigenetic mechanism governs HER2 plasticity. Here we will leverage innovative single cell epigenetics and
transcriptomics to examine the role of the epigenome in maintaining HER2 intratumoral heterogeneity, with the
long-term goal to reprogram tumors to support a therapeutically actionable reservoir of HER2-low cells.

title: The Human DNA virome: from petabase scale to single-cell resolution
text:
Though DNA viruses infect every human, most individuals do not show any initial symptoms, yet others
develop complex diseases. Here, we will develop new data science and experimental methods to understand
why individuals respond differently to the same infections by mapping the individuals, tissues, and cells that
harbor latent viruses. Applications of our new methods will uncover new interactions between the viruses and
host genetics, individual cells, and human phenotypes—all key ingredients in understanding the impact of the
human DNA virome on health and disease.

title: Rapid, Instrument-free and High Sensitivity Over-the-counter Urine Fentanyl Testing
text:
We propose to develop and commercialize the first regulatory approved over-the-counter test for
rapid, sensitive and instrument-free fentanyl detection, using our InstaStrip technology. The
resources developed in this proposal will serve as a blueprint to allow us to quickly modify the
technology for other analytes and respond rapidly to emerging drug threats.

title: Cortical oscillatory dynamics and decision deficits in suicidal behavior - Resubmission
text:
When faced with a crisis, some people but not others transition from thinking about suicide to acting on these
thoughts. This project will use a formal theoretical framework combined with electroencephalography to test
the hypothesis that individuals at risk for suicide become cognitively overwhelmed under challenging life
circumstances and make poor choices as a result. The anticipated impact of this proposal includes the
identification of more precise targets for cognitive clinical interventions.

title: Computation-guided Upper airway REhabilitation using Stanford Orthodontic Airway Plate Treatment for Pierre Robin Sequence (CURES for PRS)
text:
Infants with Pierre Robin Sequence (PRS) who experience life-threatening airway obstruction and oral
feeding difficulties often require prolonged hospitalizations and invasive surgeries such as tracheostomy or
mandibular distraction. Since 2019, we have offered the only validated non-surgical alternative—the
Stanford Orthodontic Airway Plate (SOAP)– which corrects airway obstruction and feeding challenges to
enable early discharge home through its in-person clinical assessment and manual construction of SOAP,
creating geographic challenges for infants in need. Hence, we propose to develop a sophisticated and novel
high-fidelity three-dimensional virtual airway model resulting in a scalable digital SOAP generation and
application thereby enhancing workflow, facilitating remote application, reducing healthcare cost and
disparity, and improving quality of life in infants with PRS.

title: Mechanistic insights into multifaceted roles of coronavirus exoribonuclease complex
text:
Coronavirus exoribonuclease (ExoN) complex is essential for the virus life cycle and represents a promising
target for anti-coronavirus therapies. However, many fundamental aspects of this unique enzyme remain
uncharacterized. This proposed research program aims to delineate the structural and molecular basis of
multiple key processes mediated by ExoN complex during SARS-CoV-2 genome replication and transcription,
which will provide insights into the development of new therapeutic strategies to fight the current and future
coronaviruses.

title: Mapping and Manipulating Cancer-Associated Neuronal Networks
text:
The nervous system is known to actively promote tumor growth, invasion, and treatment resistance. The
proposed project aims to expand this field and acquire a neural circuit-level understanding of how cancer and
the nervous system interact. It uses highly specialized neuroscience tools to explore how cancer might
remodel neuronal populations and exploits bidirectional interactions for its gain.

title: Targeting HIV-specific CAR T cells to the gut for the durable remission of HIV
text:
Despite the use of anti-viral drugs, HIV remains a chronic infection that decreases normal lifespan.
Curing HIV+ individuals is a top priority. We will test a new therapy in SIV-infected non-human
primates, that targets virus in both lymph nodes and the intestines to eliminate virus from the
areas it is most commonly found. This may be a cure strategy for HIV+ people.

title: CXCL5-CXCR2 Signaling in Macrophage Cholesterol Efflux and Atherosclerosis: From Mechanism to Therapy
text:
Atherosclerosis, driven by lipid accumulation and immune dysfunction in arterial walls, is regulated by the
CXCL5-CXCR2 signaling pathway, which enhances macrophage cholesterol efflux and reduces plaque
progression. This research, utilizing multi-omics, single-cell profiling, and preclinical models, elucidates the
mechanisms and therapeutic potential of CXCL5 in preventing and reversing atherosclerosis, addressing a
critical unmet need in cardiovascular disease management through novel immune-based strategies.

title: Metabolic regulation of immunosuppressive myeloid cells in the tumor microenvironment of pancreatic cancer.
text:
An immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) in pancreatic cancer, one of the deadliest human
malignancies, is known to be a major barrier to effective treatment. We propose to study how cellular interaction
within the pancreatic TME through CCR1-IRG1 axis contributes to pancreatic carcinogenesis and explore the
therapeutic potential of targeting IRG1, using both mouse models and patient derived organoids. Our study will
not only provide critical insights into the immune suppressive function of CCR1-IRG1 axis in pancreatic cancer,
thereby addressing a significant knowledge gap in the field, but also identify novel therapeutic approaches to
effectively treating pancreatic cancer.

title: 3D Printed Silicon Nitride Porous PEEK Composite Spinal Cages for Anti-Infection
text:
Up to 12% of spinal fusion surgeries fail due to infection, resulting in substantial personal and financial costs.
This study is designed to complete the development of a spinal fusion device that includes a new composite of
PEEK, a common material used to stabilize spinal fusions, plus silicon nitride, a medical implant material with
excellent antibacterial and bone integration properties. Commercialization of an antimicrobial spinal fusion device
is expected to substantially reduce the incidence of spinal fusion failure due to infection, potentially saving
hundreds of millions of dollars annually and improving patient outcomes and quality of life.

title: A triple quadrupole LC MS/MS mass spectrometer for pharmaceutical research
text:
LC MS/MS is a sophisticated high-end instrument required for biomedical and
pharmaceutical research for novel drug synthesis and detecting drug molecules in
blood/organs. It will be very useful for the faculties and graduate students working in the area
of cancer, infectious diseases, and neurodegenerative diseases. Availability of such an
instrument strengthens the research and education environment at the university.

title: Mechanistic investigations of tryptophan catabolites for vision improvement in Multiple Sclerosis
text:
Ocular pathologies and vision loss are prevalent but understudied problems of numerous autoimmune
diseases including multiple sclerosis (MS), neuromyelitis optica (NMO), uveitis, and Sjogren’s syndrome. The
proposed studies are designed to characterize metabolites and mechanisms underlying the efficacy of a
therapeutic diet to mitigate autoimmune-mediated ocular deficits in a mouse model of MS.
